memos.headline: S09 and S01 Stand Out as Relative Strength Leaders in a Broadly Oversold Tape
memos.body: I see a market where nearly every name in our universe is trading well below its 50-day and 200-day averages, with RSIs in the 30s and drawdowns of 17-22% from 52-week highs. The clear standout is S09 at 111.90, the only name above its 50-day mean (+2.4%), with an RSI of 56.2, a shallow -10.7% drawdown, and dominant relative strength vs SPY of +11.2% over 4 weeks and +7.8% over 12 weeks. S01 is the second-best technically, sitting right at its 50-day mean with only a -6.5% drawdown and strong relative strength (+5.9% 4w, +5.0% 12w). On the avoid side, S08 (RSI 31.1, -10.7% in one week, -7.1% 12w relative strength) and S06 (RSI 32.1, -15.9% over 4 weeks, -8.2% 4w relative strength) are in freefall with no sign of stabilization. I would need to see S08 reclaim 220 and S06 reclaim 245 before reconsidering those names.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+11.2% 4w vs SPY), above 50d mean, RSI 56 — trend intact; would reassess below 108.
Shallowest drawdown (-6.5%), sitting on 50d/200d means, solid relative strength vs SPY; risk level is 162.
RSI 31, down 10.7% in one week, well below both moving averages with negative relative strength — classic breakdown; need reclaim of 220 to reconsider.
RSI 32, worst 4-week return in the universe at -15.9%, and -8.2% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks despite still being above 200d mean — momentum collapse.
Nearly -20% off highs, RSI 37, -10.8% below 50d mean — deeply oversold but no reversal signal yet; would need a close above 172 to turn neutral.
Strong +8% weekly bounce but still -5.9% below 50d mean and high ATR of 6.35% makes conviction low; watching for follow-through above 128.
RSI 42 and -8.4% below 200d mean suggest a broken intermediate trend, but 4w relative strength vs SPY is +2.3% — mixed signals, need close above 410.
Deepest drawdown in the universe at -21.8% and -10.3% below 200d mean, but relative strength vs SPY is flat — could be basing but no confirmation yet.

memos.headline: S10's 56% Net Margin and 78% Revenue Growth Stand Out; S02 and S09 Show Earnings-Power Weakness
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in S10, which posted $39.3B in revenue (+77.9% YoY) with a staggering 56.2% net margin and only $8.5B in total debt—a pristine balance sheet for that scale. S05 and S04 also impress with net margins of 27.5% and 34.6% respectively, double-digit revenue growth, and manageable leverage. On the other end, S02 delivered $100.8B in revenue but only a 5.5% net margin with $76.9B in debt, and S09 saw revenue decline 1.1% YoY with a thin 9.1% margin—both signal cash-flow compression risk. S03's 88.3% net income growth is eye-catching, but the 10.7% margin on $187.8B of revenue with $58B in debt tells me the earnings recovery may be cyclical rather than structural; I'd need to see margin expansion sustain above 12% to get more constructive. I would change my view on S07 if revenue declines reverse, but a -5.0% top-line print with $31.7B in debt against only $16.2B in revenue keeps me cautious.

views.note: 56.2% net margin, 77.9% YoY revenue growth, and minimal $8.5B debt make this the strongest earnings-power story in the universe.
27.5% net margin with 11.8% revenue growth and low $14.8B debt reflects durable, high-quality earnings.
34.6% net margin and 12.3% revenue growth are strong, though $45B in debt warrants monitoring relative to cash generation.
32.7% margin and 50.5% net income growth are attractive, but $401B in total debt (financial-sector leverage) limits my conviction on downside protection.
29.2% margin is solid but revenue growth of only 4% and $94.8B in debt suggest mature, slower compounding.
88.3% net income growth looks like a cyclical recovery off a low base; 10.7% margin needs to sustain above 12% for me to get constructive.
21.2% margin and 33.5% NI growth are decent, but only 2.1% revenue growth and $25.3B debt on $21.9B revenue limit upside conviction.
Revenue declining 1.1% with a 9.1% net margin and $36.8B in debt signals deteriorating earnings power.
5.5% net margin on $100.8B revenue with $76.9B debt and only 1.6% NI growth is classic cash-flow compression territory.
Revenue fell 5% YoY and $31.7B in debt nearly doubles the $16.2B revenue base—I need a top-line inflection to reconsider.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause With Sticky Inflation at 3% YoY — Favor Banks and Staples Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed in a clear pause regime: the upper bound sits at 4.50%, down 100bp over 12 months but unchanged over the last couple of months, while CPI is running +3.0% YoY with a +1.1% acceleration over just the last three months. Unemployment is stable at 4.2%, up only 30bp YoY, signaling a labor market that is softening gently but not cracking. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply to +0.33pp (up 75bp YoY), which is constructive for bank net interest margins but warns that the long end is repricing inflation persistence. I have moderate conviction that the next move is still a cut, but not until inflation prints convincingly below 3%; a hot February CPI or a jump in unemployment above 4.4% would change my regime call. In this pause-with-sticky-inflation environment, I favor banks and defensive staples while avoiding long-duration growth names most sensitive to a higher-for-longer rate path.

views.note: Banks benefit from a steepening curve (+75bp YoY in 10y-2y spread) and stable employment supporting credit quality.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a pause regime where sticky 3% inflation limits the Fed's ability to ease further.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds with 10y yields at 4.31% and no near-term rate cuts likely given 3% CPI.
High-multiple tech/growth names are vulnerable if the higher-for-longer rate path persists and inflation stays sticky.
Cyclicals face mixed signals — stable employment supports demand but sticky inflation and paused policy limit upside.
Energy is range-bound in a soft-landing scenario; no strong macro catalyst either way from current data.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Uniformly Negative Across Universe Except S01; Washout May Create Opportunity in Hardest-Hit Names
memos.body: I note that every earnings-related 8-K in our universe except S01 triggered a negative price reaction, with S10 (-8.5%), S05 (-7.3%), S04 (-6.2%), S07 (-4.6%), S03 (-4.1%), and S09 (-2.5%) all selling off on results. S01 stands alone with a +1.9% post-earnings move, suggesting differentiated sentiment. The breadth of negativity across the group tells me the market was broadly disappointed, but by mid-March the worst of the earnings-driven tone shift should be digested—meaning names like S10 and S05 that saw the steepest drops could be approaching a sentiment trough where tone can only improve. S06 has had a flurry of corporate-action filings (director changes, bylaw amendments, rights modifications) without an earnings print, which raises governance-noise risk. I have highest conviction on S01 as a relative sentiment winner and on avoiding S10 near-term given the compounding negatives of an -8.5% earnings reaction followed by a director departure filing just days ago.

views.note: Only name in the universe with a positive post-earnings reaction (+1.9%), signaling differentiated positive sentiment.
Steepest earnings selloff at -8.5% compounded by a director departure filing on 3/7, suggesting sentiment has not yet stabilized.
The -7.3% earnings drop was severe but occurred over five weeks ago; sentiment may be troughing but I lack confirming positive tone data.
A -6.2% earnings reaction and a prior director change create mixed signals; negative tone likely priced by now but no catalyst for reversal yet.
Four 8-K filings in two weeks including bylaw amendments and rights modifications generate governance noise without earnings clarity.
The -4.6% earnings reaction is now six weeks old; negative tone likely absorbed but no fresh positive signal to justify a long.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Tripling in Three Months Signals Structural Geopolitical Risk Repricing Across the Universe
memos.body: I am seeing a dramatic escalation in policy uncertainty: the EPU index at 463 is up 228% over three months and nearly doubled in the last month alone, while VIX at 24.66 has surged 79% over the same period. HY spreads have widened 72bp in three months to 3.40%, confirming that credit markets are pricing real risk, not just volatility noise. WTI crude falling 6.8% month-over-month to $66.82 despite elevated geopolitical tension suggests demand destruction fears or supply-chain reconfiguration may be dominating energy markets—this is not a typical risk-off pattern where oil spikes on conflict. I interpret this constellation as a structural shift in policy regime—likely driven by escalating trade/sanctions actions and export controls—rather than a one-quarter event, and I would need to see EPU sustainably below 250 and HY OAS back under 3.00% to reverse my cautious stance. Without granular detail on individual company exposures from the 8-K filings, I am applying a broad risk-reduction framework, favoring names with less geopolitical surface area and penalizing those with concentrated supply-chain or China-policy exposure.

views.note: Three 8-K filings in two weeks suggest active corporate activity, but without clarity on whether these relate to geopolitical exposure adjustments, I stay neutral amid the elevated policy uncertainty backdrop.
Reg FD disclosure in late January combined with the 228% three-month surge in policy uncertainty and widening HY spreads warrants caution until geopolitical headwinds clarify.
Reg FD disclosure in January provides limited visibility; the macro backdrop of VIX at 24.66 and EPU at 463 keeps me sidelined until policy direction becomes clearer.
Single 8-K with no detail on geopolitical exposure; falling oil prices and extreme policy uncertainty make it hard to take directional conviction here.
Reg FD filing in January amid a regime where HY OAS widened 72bp in three months and EPU nearly tripled suggests elevated risk; I would need policy de-escalation to turn constructive.
Early January 8-K is stale and the current macro environment—VIX up 79% in three months—demands fresh information before taking a position.

plan.summary: In a broadly oversold tape with policy uncertainty tripling and sticky inflation keeping the Fed on pause, I favor a high-cash allocation anchored by the two relative-strength leaders (S01, S09) and a modest position in fundamentally strong S04 and S05. I avoid broken-momentum names (S08, S06) and high-multiple growth (S10) where macro headwinds and negative sentiment compound.

plans.rationale: Strongest consensus across analysts: Technical (shallowest drawdown, at 50d mean, solid relative strength), Sentiment (only positive post-earnings reaction in the universe at +1.9%), and decent Fundamentals (21% margin, 33% NI growth). Geopolitics analyst is neutral but not negative. Two analysts explicitly long with 0.70 conviction each.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below 162 (Technical's risk level) or a break below the 200-day moving average would invalidate the relative-strength thesis.

plans.rationale: Technical analyst's top pick (0.85 conviction) — only name above 50d mean, RSI 56, dominant relative strength vs SPY. However, Fundamentals analyst flags declining revenue and thin 9.1% margin, and Geopolitics analyst avoids it. Sizing down due to the fundamental-technical conflict but maintaining exposure to the strongest momentum name.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below 108 (Technical's reassessment level) or further revenue deterioration in next quarterly update.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst is long (0.75) citing 34.6% net margin and 12.3% revenue growth. Technical is neutral-to-mixed but notes positive 4w relative strength vs SPY (+2.3%). Sentiment is neutral with earnings reaction likely digested. A balanced quality name at a reasonable size.
plans.changes_my_mind: Failure to close above 410 within two weeks (Technical's confirmation level) or HY spreads widening above 4.0% signaling broader credit stress.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals analyst is strongly long (0.80) on 27.5% net margin and 11.8% revenue growth. Macro analyst favors staples in a pause regime (0.60). Technical analyst avoids due to deep oversold condition with no reversal signal yet, so I size modestly and use a wider stop. Sentiment may be troughing after -7.3% earnings drop five weeks ago.
plans.changes_my_mind: Close below 155 (roughly another 6% down) confirming continued momentum collapse, or a close above 172 would increase conviction significantly.

plans.rationale: Small position in a name with 88.3% NI growth that Fundamentals views as a cyclical recovery. No strong analyst conviction either way — Technical and Sentiment are neutral. Sized small as a diversifier with a wide stop given elevated volatility.
plans.changes_my_mind: Net margin failing to sustain above 10% in next report, or a close below 190 confirming further breakdown.

Only S09 (positive momentum, relative strength) gets market_open to ensure fill. All orders carry gap guards to avoid chasing any relief rally at the open.
